messages:
elaine: heads up — just got an escalation from a customer on iOS 16.7. They start a streaming SSE generation and mid-stream (around 8–12s in) the client sees partial tokens then the connection closes with a 0-length TCP FIN. No error body from our API. Repro on their device: LTE -> toggle WiFi -> reconnect.

elaine: logs from the client side (redacted):
```
[stream] seq=0 token="This is the start of the response..."
[stream] seq=1 token=" ...continuing"
[stream] seq=2 token=" ...then stops"
network: CELLULAR->WIFI handover
socket close: FIN
http: stream closed
```

mike: can you paste the root request headers + request_id? need the request_id to check our ingress logs. :mag:

elaine: request_id=rid_20260301_6a9f7c, headers: Authorization: Bearer <redacted>, Accept: text/event-stream, Connection: keep-alive, Chunked: true. Posted in the ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-4821

jordan: @elaine thanks — first thought: client probably losing the TCP connection during the handover and the SSE client doesn't auto-retry mid-stream (most libs treat stream as single-shot). Are they using our JS SDK or a native SSE lib?

elaine: native iOS SSE wrapper (third-party). They said it doesn't attempt reconnection when stream is closed mid-response; it just surfaces a disconnect to the app. Customer asked if we can send a final error chunk instead of silent close so they can resume.

sam: grabbing ingress logs for rid_20260301_6a9f7c. Quick check: our LB (nginx proxy) shows a backend idle timeout at 30s for that route; but I see the client disconnected at ~11s. No 5xx from backend. Might be client-side TCP reset.

harpreet: mobile note — iOS handovers can tear sockets without a SIGPIPE visible to app layers when switching networks quickly. Some apps use a short application-level heartbeat to detect this and reopen streams. Do we have keepalive responses or ping events for long SSE streams?

jordan: our SSE stream emits a comment ping every 15s by default on hosted API. If their stream was short (11s) that wouldn't have triggered. For safety we could consider reducing to 8s for few clients, but that's risky for scale.

mike: next steps: 1) confirm client behavior (reconnect vs abort) 2) ask customer to try SDK wrapper that supports reconnect/resume or to implement client-level small heartbeats 3) check proxy config and upgrade connection-level keepalive to reduce false closes.

elaine: told customer: please try the websocket fallback or our SDK with auto-reconnect in the meantime; shared a short repro script and asked for a packet capture if they can. Also suggested they enable app-level retry and resume logic.

sam: FYI I opened INF-4821 and put a config experiment on a canary LB to extend proxy idle/keepalive probing to 60s for streams coming from mobile UA. deploy-bot: deploy queued.

deploy-bot: canary deploy INF-4821-proxy-keepalive-extension started to infra-canary-3 at 2026-03-01T15:43:12Z :rocket:

harpreet: also suggested to the customer we add a lightweight JSON metadata checkpoint every ~5 tokens (small cost) so a resumed client can request the rest by token index. That would need product discussion but could improve resumability.

jordan: for immediate support addendum: share these repro steps with them: 1) run on-device reproducer with logs 2) switch network quickly 3) capture tcpdump 4) attempt SDK reconnect. If they can share tcpdump we can pin whether FIN or RST originated from client or network.

elaine: customer will try SDK fallback and capture a packet trace this afternoon. Marking this thread for follow-up. I'll update INF-4821 once we get the packet capture or if they confirm SDK fixes it. :white_check_mark:
